correctness.rationale: Exact graph is the four-bit cube. A smallest-uncovered-vertex matching recursion and a distinct even-to-odd recursion both give 272 perfect matchings. Exhaustive tests of 272 times 256 subsets agree between matching-containment counting and a valid residual-vertex completion recurrence. Coordinate actions give all 384 automorphisms and eight covering matching orbits; a separate direct alternating-edge DFS agrees for all matching profiles with symmetric-difference cycle enumeration. Full cycle-edge and packing-vertex sets are distinguished; minimum forcing degree four and packing numbers 4,3,2 are exact. Two standalone programs independently replay the complete certificate. No result for higher cube dimensions is claimed.

originality.rationale: Known 272 matchings and uniform forcing number four are excluded from the new contribution and credited. The new assertion is the finer eight-orbit local forcing-subset profile and alternating-cycle disjoint-packing classification, neither implied by only the minimum forcing number, the ordinary matching polynomial, nor the general planar-bipartite forcing principle. The matching/spectrum primary literature and an extended survey were compared; an unread 2004 article full text and unindexed enumerations are explicitly residual priority risks.

value.rationale: The motivated gap is how the planar bipartite matching-forcing versus alternating-cycle packing principle fails upon passing to a nonplanar but still bipartite cube. A natural complete classification distinguishes all matchings via eight genuine forcing-subset polynomials despite their known uniform forcing number; the exact 8/32/232 packing strata show the strength and shape of the boundary. This is not a renamed textbook deduction or arbitrary small-number slice: the target is the smallest nonplanar cube and the all-matching invariant, with reproducible complete orbit representatives.
